classification.difficultyReason: Find two ground distances from separate elevation triangles, connect them in a horizontal right triangle, and interpret the bearing from Eugene toward Dillon in the correct southwest direction.

content.prompt: Dillon and Eugene are both looking at a tower of height 35 metres. Dillon is standing due south of the tower and he measures the angle of elevation from the ground to the top of the tower to be $15^\circ$. Eugene is standing due east of the tower and he measures the angle of elevation from the ground to the top of the tower to be $20^\circ$. Find, correct to one decimal place:

children.label: a
children.prompt: the distance Dillon is from the foot of the tower

answer.worked:
Let $O$ be the foot of the tower, $T$ its top, and $D$ Dillon's position. In the vertical right triangle $DOT$:
$$\begin{align*}\tan15^\circ&=\frac{35}{OD}\\OD&=\frac{35}{\tan15^\circ}\\OD&\approx130.6\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: the distance Eugene is from the foot of the tower

answer.worked:
Let $E$ be Eugene's position. In the vertical right triangle $EOT$:
$$\begin{align*}\tan20^\circ&=\frac{35}{OE}\\OE&=\frac{35}{\tan20^\circ}\\OE&\approx96.2\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: the distance between Dillon and Eugene

answer.worked:
Since Dillon is due south and Eugene due east of $O$, $\angle DOE=90^\circ$. Using the unrounded distances:
$$\begin{align*}DE^2&=OD^2+OE^2\\DE^2&=\left(\frac{35}{\tan15^\circ}\right)^2+\left(\frac{35}{\tan20^\circ}\right)^2\\DE&=\sqrt{\left(\frac{35}{\tan15^\circ}\right)^2+\left(\frac{35}{\tan20^\circ}\right)^2}\\DE&\approx162.2\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: the bearing of Dillon from Eugene

answer.short:
$216.4^\circ\text{T}$

Measure clockwise from north at Eugene's position.
answer.worked:
Let $\theta=\angle OED$, the angle south of west at Eugene's position. Using the unrounded distances:
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{OD}{OE}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{35/\tan15^\circ}{35/\tan20^\circ}\right)\\\theta&\approx53.6^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The bearing is measured clockwise from north at $E$:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing}&=270^\circ-\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{35/\tan15^\circ}{35/\tan20^\circ}\right)\\\text{Bearing}&\approx216.4^\circ\text{T}.\end{align*}$$
